dimensions.assessment: Affects all first purchasers of motor vehicles with optional safety features, as well as motor vehicle manufacturers and sellers.
dimensions.evidence: A person may not offer for sale or lease to a first purchaser an optional safety feature

dimensions.assessment: Requires sellers to unbundle safety features from non-safety features and disclose costs separately, altering sales practices without changing vehicle manufacturing standards directly.
dimensions.evidence: offers such optional safety feature for sale or lease--separately from any non-safety feature

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal appropriations are stated, though enforcement costs may fall on the FTC and state authorities who can recover costs.
dimensions.evidence: If a State prevails in any civil action under paragraph (1), the State may recover reasonable costs and attorney fees.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new federal statutory rules enforced by the FTC with rights of action for State attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission shall enforce subsection (a) in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction

dimensions.assessment: Permanent nationwide requirement taking effect 180 days after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Paragraph (1) shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific estimates of federal administrative costs or savings.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes nationwide sales and disclosure rules regarding optional safety features in motor vehicles, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and State attorneys general, affecting vehicle manufacturers, sellers, and first purchasers.
